summary: Zhonghui Cui specializes in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and sinology. Cui earned an MA from SOAS University of London and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong, where Cui held an attested post as teaching consultant in 2013.

Zhongxin Jiang was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji (~1960–1965). Jiang held posts at Peking University, the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1980–2002), and Soka University (~1999).
Zijie Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (attested 2015). In 2015, Li held a post as a JSPS DC research fellow.
Zong Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Trijang Rinpoche. He held a post at Ganden Shartse Monastery from ~1937 to 1946.

Zongsan Mou was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Peking University (~1929–1933) under Shili Xiong. Mou held posts at Zhejiang University, National Taiwan University, National Taiwan Normal University, Tunghai University, and the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies.

Zsóka Gelle is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who pursued a PhD at the University of Vienna. Gelle held posts at Tibet House Foundation, the East-West Research Institute, Eötvös Loránd University (2014–2016), and the Budapest Centre for Buddhist Studies (2014–2016).

Zuiei Ito was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1965–1970). Ito held academic posts at Rissho University (~1976–2013), the University of Tokyo, and Waseda University.

Zuiho Yamaguchi was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1953) and under Jacques Bacot and Rolf Alfred Stein. Yamaguchi held posts at Nagoya University and the University of Tokyo (1970–1986).

Zuiryu Nakamura was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Rissho University (~1937–1940) and under Susumu Yamaguchi (1944), later serving as a professor in Rissho University's Department of Buddhist Studies in 1945.

Édouard Chavannes was a scholar in sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. After studying at the École Normale Supérieure (~1885–1888), he served as a professor at the Collège de France from 1893 to 1918.

Édouard Huber was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied at the University of Paris, INALCO, and the Collège de France (~1899–1901). He held a teaching post in Chinese at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1905–1914).

Émile Benveniste was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris under Antoine Meillet. Benveniste held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1927–1972) and the Collège de France (1937–1972).

Émile Burnouf worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at the École Normale Supérieure, the French School at Athens, and under Jean-Louis and Eugène Burnouf. He held a professorship at the University of Nancy and its Faculté des lettres (~1854–1867).
Émile Senart was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and historian/archaeologist who studied under Theodor Benfey (~1867–1868). He served as president of the Société Asiatique from 1908 to 1928.

Étienne Balázs was a sinologist and historian/archaeologist who studied under Otto Franke in 1923. He held posts as a senior researcher at the CNRS in 1949 and as a professor of Chinese economic history at the University of Paris (~1949–1963).

Étienne Lamotte was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied under Louis de La Vallée Poussin, Carlo Formichi, Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, Paul Demiéville, Marcelle Lalou, and Jean Przyluski, holding major posts at KU Leuven and Université catholique de Louvain.

Ñāṇavīra Thera was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at Wellington College, St Edmund's School, and Magdalene College, he served in the Royal Artillery (1939–1941) and Intelligence Corps (1941–1945), later studying under Pelene Siri Vajirañāṇa (~1949–1955).

Ülo Valk is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Miina Härma Gymnasium and the University of Tartu (~1980–1986). He held a post at the University of Tartu (~1995) and served as an editor for Numen (~2007).
